title: Distributed Training: Data & Model Parallelism
interviewAnswer: Data parallelism replicates the model and splits batches across workers, synchronizing gradients. Model/tensor/pipeline parallelism splits the model when it no longer fits on one device. The right strategy depends on memory, communication cost and model size.
why: Large training jobs can waste most of their budget on communication or idle accelerators if parallelism is chosen poorly.
intuition: Data parallelism gives each GPU a copy of the book and different pages to study; model parallelism gives each GPU different chapters of one huge book.
deepDive: DistributedDataParallel synchronizes gradients efficiently but global batch size changes optimization dynamics. Sharding optimizer states/parameters reduces memory. Interconnect bandwidth and topology matter almost as much as FLOPs.
workedExample: Four GPUs with batch 32 each create global batch 128. If you scale from one GPU, learning rate/scheduler behavior may need re-tuning.
commonMistakes: Assuming adding GPUs gives linear speedup.
Forgetting that larger global batch size changes optimization.
followUps: When do you need tensor parallelism?
production: Benchmark scaling efficiency and checkpoint/restart behavior; distributed jobs need fault tolerance and reproducible shard/state handling.
